chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Fadalah ibn Ayyub narrated to us from al-Husayn ibn Uthman, who said: A man narrated to me from Abu Hamzah, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:

There is no drop more beloved to Allah than a drop of blood shed in the way of Allah, or a drop of tears from an eye in the darkness of the night out of fear of Allah. And there is no step more beloved to Allah than a step taken towards a near relative, or a step by which a march in the way of Allah is completed. And there is no gulp more beloved to Allah than the swallowing of anger, or a gulp by which a servant repels his calamity [with patience].
ai.seo_question: What are the most beloved drops, steps, and gulps to Allah according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In *Kitab al-Zuhd*, this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) elevates mundane physical acts—such as weeping at night, visiting kin, and swallowing anger—into profound spiritual virtues by linking them to divine love. The text emphasizes the transformative power of *zuhd* (asceticism) and *taqwa* (God-consciousness), illustrating how internal states like patience and humility manifest in external actions beloved to Allah. This aligns with the Shia scholarly tradition of viewing the body as a vessel for spiritual refinement, where even the suppression of natural impulses becomes an act of worship.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 1.Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, “Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb narrated to us from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUthmān who said, ‘A man narrated to me from Abū Ḥamzah who said, “I heard Abū Jaʿfar (a) say, ‘

There is no drop more beloved to Allah than the drop of blood [that is shed] in the way of Allah, or the teardrop that rolls down from the eye in the darkness of night, out of fear of Allah. And there is no step more beloved to Allah than the step taken towards a near relative, or a step by which a march in the way of Allah may be completed. And there is no gulp more beloved to Allah than the anger which is swallowed, or the gulp that is swallowed by a servant in response to his calamity [as he patiently bears it to please Allah].’”’”
